clue.text: Dialect actors needed for radio programme

parts.note: a broad accent or speech is a strongly regional dialect, so broad can stand for it
the actors in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: A drama needs performers who speak in regional dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD as a noun means broad speech or dialect, as in 'broad Scots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmission over the airwaves, such as a radio show, is a synonym.

clue.text: Put up a centre of Latvian nationalism

parts.note: to rig up a tent or mast is to put it up

explanation.surface: Someone erects a focal point for Latvian national feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Latvia is the natural centre of its national life.

clue.text: Regular income from a Parisian night in New York

indicators.note: the French word for night sits inside the abbreviation for New York

parts.note: nuit is the French word for night

explanation.surface: Someone draws steady money from a French evening spent in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly payment made for life or a term is a fixed recurring income.

clue.text: One who reaps the harvest from a heavy fall

explanation.surface: A harvester takes a hard tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer who grows crops is a cultivator of produce; 'come a cropper' is the idiom for taking a bad tumble.

clue.text: Revolutionary cooking device tips up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells us to read the word tips from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A rotating kitchen gadget tilts over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sounds political but means rotating: a roasting skewer turns over the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating skewer for roasting meat over a fire turns round and round.

clue.text: They cleaned up a stack on the lotteries

parts.note: a stack is a chimney rising from a roof
sweeps is short for sweepstakes, a kind of lottery

explanation.surface: Gamblers made a pile by winning on the lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaned up' suggests winning big money, but it means literally cleaning; in a down clue 'on' puts the stack above the lotteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who brushed soot from flues were the cleaners of household stacks.

clue.text: Maybe they lead through the heart of the countryside

definitions.text: Maybe they lead through the heart of the countryside

parts.words: Maybe they lead through the heart of the countryside
parts.note: plays on blood vessels running to and from the heart: major routes carry traffic through the middle of rural land

explanation.definitionFit: Main highways are named after the body's main blood vessels because they carry the bulk of traffic.

clue.text: G&S herein told recollection embodying appeal

definitions.text: G&S herein told recollection embodying appeal

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take into their body the letter for an appeal
read as re-collection, gathering the letters together again in a new order

parts.note: G and S are the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan
O is the vocative cry of appeal, as in 'O Lord'

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan story told here as a memory with an appeal in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a Gilbert and Sullivan opera; 'recollection' rearranges G, S, HEREIN and TOLD, and 'embodying' puts the O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Savoy opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, set among Venetian boatmen.

clue.text: Welcome sign of the palsy?

parts.note: a greeting gesture read as a symptom, since palsy makes the limbs tremble

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: a trembling limb is what palsy causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping palms is a greeting gesture; the question mark reads it as a trembling limb, a symptom of palsy.

clue.text: If not, it is a confession that one has no monopoly of sagacity

definitions.text: it is a confession that one has no monopoly of sagacity

explanation.surface: A modest admission that others can be clever too.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as 'others wise': other people are clever as well.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Or else' is the everyday sense; split up it says other people are sage too.

clue.text: Purposes of first-class writing

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: The goals of top-quality prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Goals or intentions are synonyms of purposes.

clue.text: Devout politicians living off immoral earnings

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the men who live this way, so a noun

parts.note: pi is a slang short form of pious, meaning devout
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Pious politicians turn out to be living on vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who take money from prostitutes are procurers who live on vice.

clue.text: In it one may keep dry sweet wine

definitions.text: In it one may keep dry

explanation.surface: A dry sweet wine sounds a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is also an old name for a dark sweet Spanish red wine; 'dry' turns out to mean out of the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas shelter keeps campers out of the rain; tent is a dark sweet Spanish red.

clue.text: Bowl when the university team is batting

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates who might make up a university side
in cricket a batting side is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: bowl while the varsity side is batting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'; 'Bowl' looks like a cricket verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A round open vessel for washing or mixing is a bowl.

clue.text: Young scout joined by an army mercenary in Angola

parts.note: a Cub is a junior Scout

explanation.surface: A boy scout teams up with a soldier of fortune in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuban troops fought in the Angolan civil war, which the clue calls mercenaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Castro's Havana sent soldiers to fight in Angola's civil war in the 1970s.

clue.text: I eat dry mash of nutritious nature

indicators.note: to mash is to crush and mix up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone eats a dry mash of something healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to diet and nourishment is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Usual procedure in breaking an itinerary

indicators.note: the word in breaks into the middle of the synonym for an itinerary

parts.note: an itinerary is a route for a journey

explanation.surface: Interrupting a travel plan is standard practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular fixed way of doing things is standard practice.

clue.text: Unfriendly house provided with access to field

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for getting over a fence into a field

explanation.surface: A house with a way into a meadow is an unwelcoming place.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonistic or inimical behaviour is unfriendly.

clue.text: Former wife got a job as a model-undraped?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

parts.words: got a job as a model
parts.note: a model who sits for an artist has posed

explanation.surface: A man's former wife became an artist's model, unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare and uncovered, an unclothed body is laid open to view.

clue.text: One doesn't make a summer drink

explanation.surface: A drink isn't enough to make a summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'one swallow doesn't make a summer', the bird arriving in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A migratory bird of the proverb; also to gulp down a drink.

clue.text: South American custom is to provide German food

parts.note: usage is established custom

explanation.surface: In South America it is the custom to serve German food.
explanation.definitionFit: A wurst, the cased meat Germany is famous for, is a German staple.

clue.text: Was familiar with new-speak

indicators.note: speak tells us the word new is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: taken as written, the word said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone was acquainted with the latest jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been acquainted with something is to have had knowledge of it.

clue.text: Talk the leg off an iron pot or a bit off the kettle

definitions.text: Talk the leg off an iron pot

explanation.surface: Talking someone's ear off, or a part of the kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk the leg off an iron pot' is an old idiom for talking endlessly, i.e. holding forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to hold forth at length; a spout is the pouring nozzle of a kettle.

clue.text: Part of the theatre brought down by Gotterdammerung

explanation.surface: Wagner's opera brings down part of the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the cheap top gallery of a theatre; Götterdämmerung, Wagner's 'Twilight of the Gods', ends with the deities destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest gallery seats are the gods; Wagner's opera ends with the destruction of Valhalla's deities.

clue.text: Ain't otherwise antagonistic

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Isn't it the opposite of hostile?
explanation.definitionFit: Opposed or against is the sense of the prefix used as a word.

clue.text: Novel companion for Nelson

explanation.surface: A book about the admiral's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma is Jane Austen's novel; Emma, Lady Hamilton, was the mistress of Admiral Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel shares its title with the name of Lady Hamilton, Nelson's lover.

clue.text: A main drama production leading to a channel contest

definitions.text: A main drama production leading to a channel contest

parts.words: A main drama production leading to a channel contest
parts.note: main is the sea, so a great naval enterprise on the main ends in a battle in the English Channel in 1588

explanation.definitionFit: The fleet of 1588 sailed from Spain and fought the English in the Channel.

clue.text: Presumably a central figure in merchandising

definitions.text: Presumably a central figure in merchandising

parts.words: Presumably a central figure in merchandising
parts.note: reads 'central figure' literally as a man in the middle, who in trade buys from producers and sells on

explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary dealer stands between the maker and the buyer in a trade chain.
